rag_samples.question: What is a Prefab in Unity and what happens when you change the Prefab asset?
rag_samples.reference: A Prefab is a reusable GameObject template stored as an asset. Changes made to the Prefab asset propagate to all of its instances in Scenes, while instances can still hold per-instance overrides.

rag_samples.question: What does the Transform component of a GameObject store?
rag_samples.reference: Every GameObject has a Transform component that stores its position, rotation, and scale.
relevant_contexts: A GameObject is an empty container until Components are attached to it. Every GameObject has a Transform component that stores its position, rotation, and scale.

rag_samples.question: Which MonoBehaviour method is the right place for physics code?
rag_samples.reference: FixedUpdate is the right place for physics code; it is called at a fixed time interval.
relevant_contexts: Awake is called once when the script instance is loaded. Start is called before the first frame update, only if the script is enabled. Update is called once per frame, and FixedUpdate is called at a fixed time interval and is the right place for physics code.

rag_samples.question: What is the difference between Awake and Start in a Unity script?
rag_samples.reference: Awake is called once when the script instance is loaded. Start is called before the first frame update, only if the script is enabled.

rag_samples.question: What does marking a Collider as a Trigger do?
rag_samples.reference: Marking a Collider as a Trigger raises OnTriggerEnter events instead of causing physical collisions.
relevant_contexts: A Rigidbody component places a GameObject under the control of the physics engine so it responds to gravity and forces. A Collider defines the shape used for collision detection; marking it as a Trigger raises OnTriggerEnter events instead of causing physical collisions.

rag_samples.question: Which render pipelines does Unity provide?
rag_samples.reference: Unity provides the Built-in Render Pipeline, the Universal Render Pipeline (URP), and the High Definition Render Pipeline (HDRP).
relevant_contexts: Materials define how a surface looks, and Shaders are the programs that compute that appearance. Unity provides the Built-in Render Pipeline, the Universal Render Pipeline (URP), and the High Definition Render Pipeline (HDRP).
